body.p: Claims 1, 10, 18, and 20 are amended. Claims 6 and 15 are canceled. Claims 1-5, 7-14, and 16-20 remain pending. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the remarks presented below.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for the telephonic interview conducted July 18, 2024. Participating in the interview were Examiner Raymond P. Dulman and Applicant's representative, Arthi Srinivasan (Reg. No. 73,675). During the interview, Applicant'srepresentative discussed the rejection of independent claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
No agreement regarding allowability was reached.

The Office Action rejected claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Thukral (U.S. Publication No. 2009/0006129, hereinafter THUKRAL) in view of Singley (U.S. Publication No. 20050187749 Al, hereinafter SINGLEY). In rejecting the independent claims, the Office asserted that paragraphs [0212] and [0213] of Thukral disclose "converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value by applying the estimated protein value to a mathematical function or by dividing the estimated value by a patient-specific conversion factor." In particular, in the rejection of claim 1, the Office asserted that "the rate of gut glucose absorption" as described in paragraph [0213] of Thukral corresponds to the "patient-specific conversion factor" recited in the independent claims.
Paragraph [0212] of Thukral states "[p]roteins and fat are converted to an equivalent

carbohydrate amount." Thukral goes on to state "[i]t is acknowledged that one of the factors that affect the rate of gut glucose absorption (i.e., the speed of the meal) is meal composition," and "implicit to the meal amount selection, the speed of the meal is accounted." (Thukral, paragraph [0213].

Applicant respectfully submits that even assuming arguendo that the rate of gut glucose absorption described in paragraph [0213] of Thukral corresponds to the patient-specific conversion factor recited in Applicant's claims (which Applicant does not concede), nowhere does Thukral disclose or suggest how protein and fat are converted to an equivalent carbohydrate

value, and makes no mention of how the rate of gut glucose absorption (which the Office asserted corresponds to the patient-specific conversion factor recited in Applicant's claims) is used to convert protein to an equivalent carbohydrate value. Instead, Thukral merely states in paragraph [0212] that "protein and fat are converted to an equivalent carbohydrate value" and Thukral provides no additional detail.

Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Thukral does not disclose or suggest "carbohydrate value by applying the estimated protein value to a mathematical function or by dividing the estimated protein value by the patient-specific conversion factor," as recited in Applicant's claims 1, 10, and 18.
However, and without conceding in the basis of the rejection, and solely to expedite
prosecution of the application, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 10, and 18 to recite, inter alia:

(Claim 1 as amended; emphasis added).
The amendments made herein to independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are similar to what was previously recited in dependent claims 6 and 15 prior to the current amendments.
In rejecting dependent claims 6 and 16, which recites "the conversion factor is

determined based on historical meal data for the patient and further based on historical glucose level data for the patient," the Office cited paragraphs [0143], [0144], [0147], [0153], and [0212]-[0213] of Thukral. (Office Action, page 6).

Applicant respectfully submits that even assuming arguendo that the rate of gut glucose absorption described in paragraph [0213] of Thukral corresponds to the "patient-specific conversion factor" recited in Applicant's independent claims (which Applicant does not concede), nowhere does Thukral disclose or suggest "the patient-specific conversion factor is determined based on predictions of glucose level rise for the patient using historical meal data and historical glucose levels of the patient," as recited in the amendments made to claims 1, 10, and 18. Rather, in Thukral, the rate of gut glucose absorption is based on meal size.
Finally, Applicant respectfully submits that paragraphs [0143], [0144], [0147], and [0153] of Thukral are entirely unrelated to conversion of a protein value to an equivalent carbohydrate value.
For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

The remarks presented herein are fully responsive to the Office Action and are sufficient to overcome the rejections presented in the Office Action. Applicant requests withdrawal of the instant rejections and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. Should any issues remain outstanding, the Examiner is urged to telephone the undersigned to expedite prosecution.
